title: Block-Local Variables
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of block-local variables in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply block-local variables in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to scope and variable reuse and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Block-Local Variables through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding block-local variables helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Block-Local Variables helps you reason about local variables inside blocks. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Local variables inside blocks. Then connect it to Semicolon-separated block-local declarations. The remaining syllabus points—Scope and variable reuse—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Block-Local Variables
content_blocks.code:
def around
  puts "start"
  yield
  puts "finish"
end
around { puts "work" }

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports block-local variables. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.text: Create a second example for block-local variables using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Scope and variable reuse), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain block-local variables, identify its place in blocks, procs, lambdas, and closures, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
